.config/taplo.toml:
# TOML formatting, reached through dprint's `exec` plugin — the only taplo config in the tree.

# One spelling of the shared exclusion set; keep it equal to dprint.json's and the hook config's exclude.
exclude = [
  # >>> dprint
  "**/*.lock",
  "**/.claude/**",
  "**/.git/**",
  "**/build/**",
  "**/dist/**",
  "**/graphify-out/**",
  # <<< dprint
  "**/.venv/**",
  "**/node_modules/**",
]
include = [ "**/*.toml" ]

[formatting]
align_comments        = true
align_entries         = true
allowed_blank_lines   = 1
array_auto_collapse   = true
array_auto_expand     = true
array_trailing_comma  = true
column_width          = 80
compact_arrays        = false
compact_entries       = false
compact_inline_tables = false
crlf                  = false
indent_entries        = false
indent_tables         = false
inline_table_expand   = true
reorder_arrays        = true
reorder_inline_tables = true
reorder_keys          = true
trailing_newline      = true
.config/pre-commit-config.yaml:
---
# The local gate; every run by hand needs `--config .config/pre-commit-config.yaml`.

minimum_pre_commit_version: "3.2.0"

default_install_hook_types:
  - pre-commit
  - commit-msg
  - post-commit
  - post-merge

# Stated once so each hook below only says what differs from it.
default_stages: [pre-commit]

# The shared exclusion set — keep it equal to dprint's and taplo's; add a tree here, never inside one hook.
# Lines after the first open with `|`; an appended block edits none above it.
exclude: |-
  (?x)
  # >>> pre-commit
  (^|/)\.claude/
  |(^|/)\.git/
  |(^|/)build/
  |(^|/)dist/
  |(^|/)graphify-out/
  |(^|/)[^/]*\.lock$
  # <<< pre-commit
  |(^|/)\.venv/
  |(^|/)node_modules/

repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: no-dash-names
        name: No path component starting with a dash
        description: Every tool the gate hooks below call reads an argument
          beginning with `-` as an option, so such a name breaks — or silently
          changes — the formatters and linters it is handed to.
        entry: Rename these files — a path component starting with a dash is
          read as an option by the formatters and linters
        language: fail
        files: '(^|/)-'

      - id: git-config
        name: Required local git-config (forge identity, ssh signing)
        description: Requires a per-repo identity equal to the forge variables
          — user.name, user.email and user.signingkey from GITHUB_*, GITLAB_*
          or GIT_* — with ssh-signed commits and tags. `--fix` writes those
          keys from the variables and unsets gpg.program and gpg.ssh.program;
          an unset variable fails the hook and writes nothing. A commit that
          changed any key is refused — git read the old identity before the
          hook ran — and the re-run carries the corrected one.
        entry: mise x -- mise run code:git-config --fix
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false
        always_run: true

      # Tool-neutral: each hook names a task. `format` runs first (it rewrites), `sec` last (it cannot fix).
      - id: format
        name: Format (mise run code:format)
        description: The repo's formatters, run over the files being committed.
          The task owns the tool list and its config paths; this hook only
          passes it the staged files.
        entry: mise x -- mise run code:format --fix
        language: system
        pass_filenames: true

      - id: lint
        name: Lint (mise run code:lint)
        description: The repo's linters, run over the files being committed.
          The task owns which linters exist for the pinned stack, and skips the
          ones whose tool or config is absent.
        entry: mise x -- mise run code:lint --fix
        language: system
        pass_filenames: true
        require_serial: true

      - id: sec
        name: Secrets (mise run code:sec --staged)
        description: The secret scan, over what is staged rather than over the
          tree. `--staged` is what selects that mode inside the task, which is
          also why no filenames are passed — the task asks git, not pre-commit,
          for the staged content.
        entry: mise x -- mise run code:sec --staged
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false
        always_run: true

      - id: graphify-refresh
        name: Refresh the graphify graph (mise run code:graph)
        description: Rebuilds the knowledge graph in the background after each
          commit and each merge or pull; the task skips a worktree, a rebase and
          a missing graphify.
        entry: mise x -- mise run code:graph
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false
        always_run: true
        stages: [post-commit, post-merge]

  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v6.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: check-added-large-files
        name: Check for added large files (>1MB)
        description: A binary committed by accident is cheap to refuse and
          expensive to remove — it stays in history after the delete.
        args: ["--maxkb=1024"]
      - id: check-case-conflict
        name: Check for case-conflicting filenames
        description: Two paths differing only in case collide on macOS and
          Windows checkouts, where one silently overwrites the other.
      - id: check-illegal-windows-names
        name: Check for filenames Windows cannot check out
        description: A path named CON, AUX or carrying a reserved character
          makes the whole clone fail on Windows, not just that file.
      - id: check-executables-have-shebangs
        name: Check that executables have shebangs
        description: An executable with no shebang runs under whatever shell
          the caller happens to have, which is how a bash script meets zsh.
      - id: check-shebang-scripts-are-executable
        name: Check that scripts with shebangs are executable
        description: The other half of the same gate, and the one that bites
          here — a task file landing 644 is reported by mise as an unknown
          task rather than as a permission error.
      - id: check-merge-conflict
        name: Check for merge conflict markers
        description: Conflict markers committed into a source file parse as
          syntax errors somewhere far from the merge that caused them.
      - id: check-symlinks
        name: Check for broken symlinks
        description: A symlink to a path that no longer exists is a silent
          nothing at read time rather than an error.
      - id: destroyed-symlinks
        name: Check for destroyed symlinks
        description: A symlink committed as a regular file containing its own
          target path — what happens when a tool without symlink support
          rewrites the tree.
      - id: check-json
        name: Check JSON syntax
        description: Every config gate below reads a config file; an unparseable
          one fails inside the tool with a message about the tool.
        # .vscode/ files are JSONC by design.
        exclude: ^\.vscode/
      - id: check-toml
        name: Check TOML syntax
        description: Same reason as JSON, for the toolchain manager's config.
      - id: check-yaml
        name: Check YAML syntax
        description: Same reason again, and it covers this file — a broken
          hook config disables the gate rather than failing it.
      - id: detect-private-key
        name: Check for committed private keys
        description: The secret scanner further down catches these too; this
          one is free and runs first, so the common case fails immediately.
      - id: end-of-file-fixer
        name: Ensure files end with a newline
        description: A missing final newline makes the next append show as a
          two-line diff and breaks line-oriented tools mid-pipeline.
      - id: trailing-whitespace
        name: Remove trailing whitespace
        description: Invisible in review and the cause of diffs nobody
          authored when the next editor strips it.
        # Two trailing spaces are a Markdown hard break.
        exclude: \.md$
      - id: mixed-line-ending
        name: Normalise line endings to LF
        description: A CRLF file entering the tree rewrites whole-file diffs
          for everyone else. `--fix=lf` settles it rather than reporting it.
        args: ["--fix=lf"]
      - id: no-commit-to-branch
        name: Refuse a direct commit to main
        description: main is what consumers read, and it takes merges only.
          Merges are unaffected — git runs `pre-merge-commit` for those.
        args: ["--branch", "main"]

  - repo: https://github.com/qoomon/git-conventional-commits
    rev: v2.9.0
    hooks:
      - id: conventional-commits
        name: Conventional Commits
        description: The commit-msg gate. The release notes are generated from
          these messages, so a type outside the convention is a change that
          silently never appears in a changelog.
        args: ["--config", ".config/git-conventional-commits.yaml"]
        stages: [commit-msg]

  # The config audit, `manual` only: both hooks fail on a correct config in a young repo.
  - repo: meta
    hooks:
      - id: check-hooks-apply
        name: Audit — every hook matches at least one file
        description: Catches a `files:` regex that stopped matching after a
          rename, which is a gate that reports success while checking nothing.
        stages: [manual]
      - id: check-useless-excludes
        name: Audit — every exclude matches at least one file
        description: Catches an exclusion whose reason expired, which is the
          failure mode nobody re-reads because it keeps working.
        stages: [manual]

  - repo: https://github.com/acme/team-hooks
    rev: v1.0.0
    hooks:
      - id: team-check

  # >>> uv
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: uv-lock-check
        name: uv lockfile is current
        entry: mise x -- uv lock --check
        language: system
        files: (^|.*/)pyproject\.toml$
        pass_filenames: false
  # <<< uv
.config/git-conventional-commits.yaml:
---
# The commit convention: the `commit-msg` hook enforces it, and the changelog reads it.

convention:
  # Ten types, and no more.
  commitTypes:
    - feat # a new capability a user can observe. Bumps the minor version.
    - fix # a defect in a shipped capability, not in one added this branch.
    - perf # same behaviour, measurably cheaper. Say what was measured.
    - refactor # neither fixes nor adds — including pure formatting changes.
    - revert # undoes an earlier commit; name it in the body.
    - test # tests only. A test written alongside a fix belongs to the fix.
    - ops # tooling, config, dependencies, CI, release mechanics.
    - docs # prose: README, guides, specifications, design documents.
    - merge # a merge commit. Written by the merge task, rarely by hand.
    - wip # work in progress. Never survives a merge; excluded from notes.
    - hotfix

  # MARKED POSITION — commitScopes: one scope per project id, filled from the `scopes` argument.
  # A scope that stops existing stays listed, marked `# retired`: deleting it invalidates its commits.
  commitScopes:
    - api

  featureCommitTypes:
    - feat

  # A repo that namespaces its tags per component narrows this to that prefix.
  releaseTagGlobPattern: "*"

changelog:
  # test, ops, docs, merge and wip are deliberately absent from the notes.
  commitTypes:
    - feat
    - fix
    - perf
    - refactor
    - revert

  includeInvalidCommits: false

  # Also catches `wip` commits written before the convention.
  commitIgnoreRegexPattern: '^[wW][iI][pP]\b'

  headlines:
    feat: Features
    fix: Bug Fixes
    perf: Performance Improvements
    refactor: Refactors
    revert: Reverts
    breakingChange: BREAKING CHANGES

  # MARKED POSITION — the changelog links, filled and uncommented from `origin`; with no remote they stay commented.
  #
  # commitUrl: <forge>/<owner>/<repo>/commit/%commit%
  # commitRangeUrl: <forge>/<owner>/<repo>/compare/%from%...%to%?diff=split
  # issueRegexPattern: "#[0-9]+"
  # issueUrl: <forge>/<owner>/<repo>/issues/%issue%
.config/linter.yaml:
---
# The house linter's config — zero-config without it, and shipped empty of overrides.

version: 1

# Generated trees only — the linter does not read .gitignore.
ignores:
  # >>> pre-commit
  - "**/build/"
  - "**/graphify-out/"
  # <<< pre-commit
  - "**/.venv/" # package-manager/uv

# overrides:
#   typescript:
#     rules:
#       "@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any": "error"
#
# configs:
#   - name: "custom"
#     files: ["**/*.ts"]
#     rules: {}
.config/gitleaks.toml:
title = "Repository secret-scanning rules"

# Never delete `useDefault`: without it this file replaces gitleaks' built-in rules.
[extend]
useDefault = true

# Custom rules go here, one per credential shape the defaults miss:
#
# [[rules]]
# description = "<vendor> API key"
# id          = "<vendor>-api-key"
# regex       = '''<prefix>_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}'''
# tags        = [ "api-key", "<vendor>" ]

# Generated trees only (`gitleaks dir` ignores .gitignore) — never tracked source, a rule id or `.env`.
[allowlist]
paths = [
  # >>> gitleaks
  '''(^|/)build/''',
  '''(^|/)dist/''',
  '''(^|/)graphify-out/''',
  # <<< gitleaks
  '''(^|/)\.venv/''',
]
.config/grype.yaml:
---
# grype's config; `code:sec` passes `--config .config/grype.yaml`.

# Change together with `code:sec`'s `--fail-on medium`; never lower it to clear a first scan.
fail-on-severity: medium

# Each entry carries a comment above it: the id, the package and version, why it does not apply, and when it expires.
ignore:
  # GHSA-aaaa-bbbb-cccc in left-pad@1.0.0: never reached; re-check 2027-01-01
  - vulnerability: GHSA-aaaa-bbbb-cccc
